product_tiers.notes: OAuth registration is self‑serve with no review required.

summary: Calendly provides a self‑serve OAuth registration portal that requires login via GitHub or Google, supports standard scopes without review, and issues tokens that expire after 30 days.

time.setup_notes: Official docs do not publish an estimated setup time.

approval_wait.label: None for basic install · Marketplace: not published
approval_wait.notes: Calendly does not require an OAuth app review; no public wait time is documented.

prerequisites.item: Calendly developer account (sign‑up with GitHub or Google)
prerequisites.notes: Login is required to access the OAuth app creation page.

steps.title: Create a Calendly developer account
steps.detail: Visit the developer portal and sign up using GitHub or Google credentials.

steps.title: Register a new OAuth application
steps.detail: In the portal, click “Create a new OAuth application”, provide a name, select environment (Sandbox or Production), and enter a redirect URI (HTTPS for Production, HTTP localhost allowed for Sandbox).

steps.title: Select required scopes
steps.detail: Choose from users:read, webhooks:read, webhooks:write, scheduled_events:read based on the functionality needed.

steps.title: Save the client ID and client secret
steps.detail: After registration, copy the generated client ID and client secret for use in your application.

steps.title: Implement OAuth flow
steps.detail: Use the authorization endpoint https://auth.calendly.com/oauth/authorize and token endpoint https://auth.calendly.com/oauth/token with PKCE (S256) to obtain access tokens.

claims_evidence.claim: Calendly provides an OAuth app registration page at https://developer.calendly.com/docs/authentication/creating-an-oauth-app.
claims_evidence.supporting_quote: Create a new OAuth application + Provide name of your application + Select the kind of application (web or native) + Select your environment that you want to associate your application Sandbox Production

claims_evidence.claim: Redirect URIs must use HTTPS for Production environments and may use HTTP only for localhost in Sandbox.
claims_evidence.supporting_quote: Redirect URI: For the Sandbox environment, we allow HTTP with localhost domain. Example: For the Production environment, this must be HTTPS

claims_evidence.claim: Calendly OAuth tokens expire after 30 days.
Calendly does not require an OAuth app review for standard scopes.
Supported scopes are users:read, webhooks:read, webhooks:write, scheduled_events:read.
